GNI_STAR: CSO Annual National Accounts 2023 reports €290.9bn. This is the recorded release vintage, not a claim about the latest revision.
NORTH_GNI: Uses the recorded £63.3bn project anchor and divides by verified 2023 GBP-per-EUR .86979. The official GDP cell and vintage remain unverified, so this anchor supports experiments only.
UK_2019_TO_2023_EUR: Uses the original sterling figures, ONS L8GG calendar-year averages for 2019 and 2023, and the reciprocal of the verified annual ECB reference rate. No reverse conversion of rounded euro totals.
UK_FY2022_TO_2023_EUR: ONS L8GG FY2022–23 to CY2023 conversion with recorded 2023 FX. Whether this is the correct fiscal period of the frozen study observations remains unresolved.
BASE_REVENUE: Doyle 2025 Table 1 reports revenue £21.773bn. The same assumed FY conversion as the frozen bridge is used. Exact official release and cell need confirmation.
BASE_SPENDING: Opening revenue plus the frozen €17.058bn deficit. It reconciles exactly to the project deficit and approximates the separately rebased study spending figure within source rounding.
GROSS_PAY_FULL: F&M 2024 Table 6 gives a 2019 gross pay increment of £4.306bn. It is separately rebased, not inferred from a net fiscal envelope or treated as a current wage-policy costing.
GROSS_WELFARE_FULL: F&M 2024 Table 6 gives a 2019 gross welfare increment of £4.809bn. Eligibility, composition and future rates still require programme costing.
SOURCE_PAY_BASE: F&M 2024 Table 6 reports a 2019 current public pay bill of £6.797bn. It is a historical normalisation, not a newly measured Northern Ireland pay bill.
PUBLISHED: Doyle 2025 Table 1 and Table 2 contain £14.220bn. Table 2 labels the period 2019 while Table 1 and surrounding text say 2023. The official update remains on hold.
PENSIONS: Doyle 2025 Table 2 reports £5.722bn. The same frozen envelope now defines both immediate transfer and the endpoint of phased funding transfer, without mixing a net incremental allowance with a different gross endpoint.
DEBT_INT: Doyle 2025 Table 2 reports £3.533bn. It remains a frozen annual interest-flow scenario, not an allocated inherited debt principal or refinancing forecast.
DEFENCE_NET: Doyle 2025 Table 2 reports £1.367bn. The accepted share starts at zero, and any assumed deduction is explicit. Replacement security and defence services still need costing.
OTHER_NONID: Doyle 2025 Table 2 reports £0.400bn overseas and £0.177bn central costs. The accepted share starts at zero. Replacement functions and EU costs need a programme budget.
TAX_ADD: Doyle 2025 Table 2 combines £0.500bn HQ, £0.265bn central spending and £0.769bn tax/PRSI changes. The accepted share starts at zero. Attribution is not automatically additional cash revenue.
RERATE_FULL: F&M 2024 Table 7 original sterling 2019 difference £18.104bn minus £9.577bn, converted directly with the UK deflator and recorded FX. The gap between this net increment and Table 6 gross components is kept visible rather than allocated to household income.

parameterAudit.investmentCapitalShare: Explicit split of additional expenditure. Starts at zero so current services and welfare never automatically become productive capital.
parameterAudit.spareCapacity: Chosen capacity margin. Starts at zero. Demand cannot create real output above the selected fixed-price capacity limit.
parameterAudit.growthRevenue: Off by default. Enabling this applies an assumed marginal revenue share to extra output, without claiming an estimated fiscal effect.
parameterAudit.taxShare: Explicit marginal revenue assumption. No average tax ratio is automatically treated as a causal tax elasticity.
parameterAudit.baselineRevenueGrowth: Explicit real receipts path. Constant in real terms by default, not automatically tied to assumed output convergence.
parameterAudit.baselineSpendingGrowth: Explicit real spending path. Constant in real terms by default. Any ageing already in this path must not be added again.
parameterAudit.defenceSavingShare: Accepted share of the study deduction, zero by default. A negotiation scenario, not an agreed saving.
parameterAudit.centralSavingShare: Accepted share of the study central and overseas deductions, zero by default. Replacement functions remain a costing question.
parameterAudit.taxAdjustmentShare: Accepted share of study revenue adjustments, zero by default. This must be reconciled to the tax base and harmonisation assumptions.
parameterAudit.pensionTransferYears: Linear transfer of the same pension funding envelope. Forty years follows a stylised period discussed by Doyle, not a cohort forecast or agreed settlement.
parameterAudit.ageSensitiveSpending: Explicit additional non-pension service spending exposed to ageing. Zero until a programme base is supplied. Excludes ageing already in baseline spending.
parameterAudit.outputCeiling: Optional numerical scenario bound, disabled by default. It is not measured parity with the Republic. A run records when it binds.
parameterAudit.baselineGrowth: No estimated counterfactual or confidence interval. Distinguish output growth, productivity growth and population growth.
parameterAudit.investmentEfficiency: No NI project-level delivery estimate. Spending called investment also includes recurring health, education and welfare in Doyle Table 3, so it cannot all become productive physical capital.
parameterAudit.investmentLag: Chosen timing with all expenditure completing at one lag. No project pipeline or distributed completion profile.
parameterAudit.capitalDepreciation: No asset mix or independently measured stock. Different public and private assets should not automatically share a depreciation rate.
parameterAudit.publicCapitalRatio: No measured NI reference public capital stock. The elasticity cannot identify an output effect without a defensible stock denominator.
parameterAudit.publicCapitalElasticity: Bom and Ligthart report an average .106 across heterogeneous studies. It is not a NI causal coefficient and may overlap private-capital and employment responses added separately.
parameterAudit.privateCapitalRatio: Unmeasured reference stock. Results depend on this scale and on whether the stock is gross or net.
parameterAudit.privateCrowdIn: Unestimated response. Public-capital effects may already include private adjustment, creating overlap.
parameterAudit.privateAdjustment: Unestimated adjustment speed. The net additional stock now adjusts directly towards its target, with replacement implicit. It is a diagnostic and does not add another GDP effect.
parameterAudit.privateCapitalElasticity: Chosen Cobb–Douglas exponent, not an estimated NI capital share. It is used only for a private-productivity diagnostic and does not add to headline GDP.
parameterAudit.payShare: Unverified pay/welfare split. A net fiscal harmonisation envelope cannot be split into gross household income without tax and benefit reconciliation.
parameterAudit.publicPayBase: A rebased historical pay-bill benchmark from F&M Table 6 replaces the invented normalisation. It is not a current measured NI pay bill or an estimate of private wage spillovers.
parameterAudit.payDisposableShare: Illustrative after-tax share. Fiscal feedback from the pay increase has not been reconciled to the net harmonisation envelope.
parameterAudit.payMPC: No recipient-specific consumption estimate. Tax financing and displaced Republic spending are absent.
parameterAudit.welfareMPC: No recipient-specific consumption estimate or saving dynamics. Benefit eligibility and withdrawal rates are absent.
parameterAudit.domesticRetention: No input-output estimate of imports or flows between NI, the Republic and Great Britain. Domestic geography must be defined.
parameterAudit.demandRealisation: Unestimated spare-capacity closure. The first-round response is capped by the selected spare capacity. This is a fixed-price experiment, not a general-equilibrium closure.
parameterAudit.wageSpillover: Unestimated public-to-private wage transmission. Labour groups, occupations and regional wage bargaining are not represented.
parameterAudit.labourSupplyElasticity: The UCD paper does not estimate this aggregate NI coefficient. Household-specific wage elasticities cannot be directly treated as an aggregate employment effect.
parameterAudit.welfareIncomeElasticity: Chosen income effect without benefit withdrawal or substitution effects. The income base is a hard-coded share of output.
parameterAudit.labourDemandElasticity: Chosen response to a productivity-minus-wages index. No firm first-order conditions, labour share or NI estimation establish it.
parameterAudit.labourSlack: No observed labour-force, hours, skills or participation constraint. Fixed reference employment does not grow with the baseline economy.
parameterAudit.publicRecruitmentElasticity: A diagnostic index only. No measured staff response, vacancy closure, staffing cost or public-service benefit.
parameterAudit.baselineEmployment: Illustrative scale rather than verified employment. Additional jobs should be called job equivalents, not a forecast.
parameterAudit.migrationResponse: Migration responds only to unfilled jobs. Housing, departures, return migration, composition and fiscal incidence are omitted.
parameterAudit.migrantHouseholdSize: Chosen household scale with no age structure. No separate children, retirees or secondary earners.
parameterAudit.serviceCostPerResident: Chosen marginal cost, not a budget costing. Housing, capital infrastructure and congestion are absent.
parameterAudit.gNI: Chosen policy output growth, not a treatment effect estimated from reunification. It must exclude the linked mechanisms and residual shocks to avoid counting gains twice.
parameterAudit.southGrowth: Chosen Republic real GNI* path. It changes the denominator only and does not represent spillovers or financing effects on Republic activity.
parameterAudit.ageing: Applies to the pension envelope and an explicitly supplied service base. Zero initially. It is not a demographic projection and must not duplicate baseline spending growth.
parameterAudit.shift: Assumed disappearance of part of the deficit without an identified causal or accounting mechanism.
parameterAudit.realInterest: Constant real marginal borrowing rate. No debt-risk premium, maturity structure, inflation surprise or fiscal response.
parameterAudit.discountRate: Chosen real discount rate. Discounted financing-inclusive costs are a cash-flow measure, not a social welfare valuation.
parameterAudit.businessUplift: Residual assumed output-level effect, not an FDI estimate. No firm entry, profit repatriation, trade model or corporation-tax base.
parameterAudit.labourUplift: A separately assumed residual labour output contribution in either configuration, not output calculated from diagnostic job equivalents. It must exclude effects already represented by other mechanisms.
parameterAudit.transitionShock: Chosen temporary output loss. No currency, banking, border, trade diversion or confidence model identifies its size.
parameterAudit.privateMaturity: Chosen linear phase-in, not estimated business adjustment.
parameterAudit.privateRecovery: Chosen linear recovery, not an estimated transition path.
parameterAudit.fundOpening: Existing assets are an endowment. Prior taxation, forgone public investment and alternative uses are outside the horizon.
parameterAudit.fundReturn: Deterministic real return without risk, fees or covariance with borrowing costs. A favourable return spread is not free fiscal capacity.
parameterAudit.fundContribution: Asset acquisition, normally financed by taxes or borrowing. The model correctly adds financing needs but has no macro financing feedback.
parameterAudit.fundContributionYears: Chosen saving horizon. No fiscal rule or legal mandate is represented.
parameterAudit.fundDrawCap: Chosen withdrawal ceiling. Not a sustainable spending rule or guarantee of available assets.
parameterAudit.investment: Preset spending choice. Capital versus current expenditure, additionality, maintenance and procurement capacity need separate budgets.
parameterAudit.duplication: Preset recurring cost without a functional cost study or time-dependent transition budget.
parameterAudit.reratingScope: Chosen harmonisation scope. Benefits, eligibility, staffing, hours and service quality are compressed into one envelope.
parameterAudit.reratingYears: Chosen linear schedule. The source does not identify a single pay and welfare convergence process.
parameterAudit.pensionsUK: Negotiated scenario, not a settled legal or actuarial result. The current UI wording is qualified.
parameterAudit.debtUK: Negotiated scenario, not a settled allocation of debt stock, assets or interest.
parameterAudit.stall: After year seven the relative rate is capped at the lower of its previous rate and .4%. It cannot accelerate a low-growth path, but the timing and cap remain scenario assumptions.
parameterAudit.linkedMechanisms: Research configuration. Enabling links creates an illustrative mechanism experiment, not an estimated causal model.
parameterAudit.horizon: Reporting choice rather than evidence. Long horizons magnify unsupported persistence, missing terminal liabilities and the output ceiling.

relationships: The opening accounting reference has no negotiated deductions, no additional growth revenue and no linked behavioural effects. It is a conditional reference, not a best estimate of transition costs.
Net harmonisation uses original sterling Table 7 values directly. Gross pay and welfare use separate Table 6 values. All use the same recorded UK deflator and FX convention.
Gross pay and welfare no longer come from an arbitrary split of a net fiscal envelope. The source gross/net discrepancy is recorded without inventing its composition.
Separate gross receipts and spending paths reconcile to the frozen deficit. Growth in output does not silently generate revenue. Both real fiscal growth rates are explicit.
Each disputed defence, central-spending and revenue adjustment has an explicit accepted share, initially zero. The UK pension and debt switches are independent of policy labels.
A single pension envelope transfers linearly over the selected period. Phased and immediate transfer agree at the endpoint, without mixing gross and net conventions or claiming a cohort projection.
Ageing applies to pensions and an explicit non-pension service base. No arbitrary share of a residual deficit is aged and no residual balance disappears through composition.
Only the explicitly selected capital share of additional expenditure can become productive capital. That share starts at zero. Maintenance and project selection remain uncosted.
Public capital provides one reduced-form output effect. Induced private capital and jobs are diagnostics, not extra output multipliers stacked on that benchmark.
The additional net stock moves towards its target with replacement implicit. There is no second depreciation deduction preventing convergence to a fixed target.
Real demand effects cannot exceed selected spare capacity. The fixed-price experiment has no estimated price, trade, monetary or Republic-financing response.
The marginal revenue rate is adjustable and feedback is off initially. Policy growth and residual shocks must exclude effects entered in other channels.
There is no implicit doubling ceiling or claim of income parity. An optional user-selected bound records each binding year.
The switch never raises the relative growth rate after year seven. Its timing and remaining cap are still scenario settings.
Policy selection does not mutate liability switches. All compared bundles use the same negotiated terms, growth and structural settings. The selected comparison line uses exactly the main-run inputs.
A downloaded run includes policy inputs, shared settings, all compared bundles, annual results and the executable fingerprint. A CLI rejects mismatched models or results.
Contributions acquire assets and increase financing needs. Withdrawals reduce financing, not spending. Surpluses repay debt and excess becomes cash. Opening assets are not free income.
A constant annual interest allocation is not a negotiated debt stock. No inherited principal or refinancing model has been invented.
Wage spillovers, labour supply, welfare income effects and firm labour demand remain unestimated. Their indices cannot establish changes in employment or public-service quality.
Optional migration adds residents and service costs. No return migration, cohort ageing, housing constraint or complete migrant tax account is estimated.
UK status quo is zero only from the incremental Republic perspective. Shared Island allocates its extra expenditure to the Republic. No welfare ordering or constitutional causal effect follows.
The frozen ONS fiscal baseline and its exact official cells remain on hold. A historical harmonisation benchmark combined with a later deficit is a hybrid scenario, not an updated policy costing.
No probabilities, distributional microsimulation, banking model, currency changeover, trade model or complete all-island welfare analysis is supplied. Slider bounds are not confidence intervals.

unitary.name: Unitary
unitary.desc: Full absorption on day one. Welfare and pay harmonise immediately, duplication ends fast, with growth selected independently.

federal.name: Federal
federal.desc: A continuing Stormont inside an all-island state. Full harmonisation phased over two decades, but two administrations run permanently.

glide.name: Managed Integration
glide.desc: An illustrative linear harmonisation schedule with additional expenditure during the first decade. Growth is a separate assumption.

worst.name: Higher initial cost
worst.desc: Immediate pay and welfare harmonisation without additional investment. Liability choices and growth are controlled separately and apply to every policy bundle.

statusquo.name: UK status quo
statusquo.desc: Northern Ireland remains in the UK. Its regional deficit remains UK-funded. No incremental Republic expenditure is assumed.

shared.name: Shared Island
shared.desc: Northern Ireland remains in the UK. The Republic funds the investment selected below. UK liabilities do not transfer.

assumptions: Reference case

Initial policy growth equals the NI output reference growth. Extra-output revenue and linked mechanisms are off. No negotiated deduction or liability retention is assumed. This is an accounting reference, not a best estimate.
Policy selection
Only policy expenditure, timing and harmonisation controls reset. Negotiated terms, growth and slowdown stay common across bundles. No preset mutates a liability switch.
Prices
Original sterling observations are converted with the recorded UK GDP deflator and reciprocal 2023 annual sterling-per-euro rate. Net and gross harmonisation source rows are separate.
Vintage

The official fiscal update remains on hold. FY2022–23 is the recorded conversion assumption for the frozen study fiscal inputs. The model has relative years and does not forecast a calendar transition date.
Gross baseline
Receipts and spending have independent real growth settings. Zero means a constant real fiscal baseline, not a forecast that services or tax bases will remain unchanged.
Deductions

Selected percentages apply separately to defence, central/overseas spending and tax adjustments. Their initial values are zero. The study itemised adjustments sum to £12.733bn, not the printed £12.773bn total.
Pensions

One frozen pension envelope defines both immediate and phased funding costs. If the UK retains accrued liabilities, the Republic funds min(t/transferYears,1) of the envelope. This is not a cohort model and no new tax recovery is invented.
Inherited interest
The negotiated envelope is a constant real annual flow. It is not an inherited debt principal and is separate from new transition borrowing.
Ageing

A selected ageing factor applies to the pension envelope and an explicitly supplied non-pension service spending base. The extra service base must exclude ageing already represented in baseline spending growth. Default ageing and extra service base are zero.
Composition
There is no automatic erosion of the residual deficit. Non-zero legacy shift inputs are rejected.
Harmonisation

The net fiscal envelope and the gross pay and welfare increments phase in linearly on the same selected schedule. The gross/net source discrepancy remains a reconciliation boundary, not an assumed household income split or an extra tax gain.
Pay benchmark
The pay-bill normalisation uses the historical F&M table rather than an invented current wage bill. Future real wage growth and occupational comparability are not separately modelled.
Additional expenditure
Expenditure lasts ten years. Only its selected capital share can become productive capital, after the selected completion lag and efficiency loss. The capital share starts at zero.
Public capital

Completed investment is depreciated each subsequent year. Its denominator is a chosen reference stock ratio. The external output elasticity is a transferred reduced-form benchmark, not a NI causal estimate.
Private capital

The additional net stock adjusts towards the selected target over the adjustment period, with replacement implicit. Target increments are bounded between minus and plus 50% of reference stock, with a lower stock bound of minus 80%.
Avoiding induced-output overlap
Private capital, job equivalents and recruitment are diagnostics in the linked experiment. They do not multiply the reduced-form public-capital output dividend again.
Consumption

Gross pay is reduced by the disposable-pay share, then pay and welfare propensities, retention and realisation determine first-round demand. Capacity limits the realised effect. No complete tax-financing or price model is implied.
Capacity
Output including demand cannot exceed supplyOutput/(1−spareCapacity/100) before separate residual output shocks. Default spare capacity is zero.
Labour diagnostics

Wage spillovers and labour supply/demand coefficients are unestimated. The welfare income normalisation is 0.6 times reference output. Changes are bounded between minus and plus 50% of reference employment.
Recruitment
An index bounded at 150 with base 100. It is not actual staffing, a service outcome or extra output.
Migration
Optional unfilled job demand attracts migrant residents and marginal service costs. There is no return migration, housing constraint or full migrant tax account. Migration starts at zero.
Residual shocks

Business and labour residuals phase in linearly, while disruption decays linearly from year one. Residuals must exclude effects already included in policy growth or other mechanisms. All start at zero.
Revenue feedback
Additional output generates no fiscal revenue unless the separate growthRevenue switch is enabled. The marginal rate is an assumption, not the average revenue ratio or an estimated elasticity.
Slowdown
After year seven relative growth uses min(previous relative rate,1.004), so the switch can never accelerate a path. Timing and the cap remain illustrative.
Output bounds

The default has no economic output ceiling. A selected positive ceiling is a multiple of NI reference output, not measured Republic parity. Output is floored at zero and binding ceilings are recorded.
Fiscal perspective

UK status quo has zero incremental Republic cost. Shared Island charges its extra expenditure and financing to the Republic. Regional gross fiscal paths are recorded separately and do not imply welfare rankings.
Fund order
Returns accrue on opening assets, withdrawals follow, then contributions enter the fund. Withdrawals are bounded by positive costs, assets and the selected cap.
Contributions
Asset purchases increase financing needs and assets equally. They can be debt-financed in this accounting model, without assuming beneficial macroeconomic feedback.
Fund risk

Constant real returns can be negative. No volatility, fees, asset allocation, correlation or risk-adjusted return premium is estimated. Opening assets have prior funding and opportunity costs outside the horizon.
Cash and debt
Surpluses repay debt first and excess becomes zero-return cash. Cash is used before new borrowing. Debt is floored at zero.
Wealth identity
Change in net liabilities equals cumulative financing-inclusive costs minus cumulative fund returns. Adding opening assets back avoids treating an endowment as free income.
Present value
Costs include transition interest and are discounted at end-year real rates. This cash-flow present value excludes fund contributions, draws and fund returns and is not a social valuation.
Break-even
Unrounded sign flags determine the first non-positive annual cost and the first cumulative crossing after positive costs. Neither is a discounted welfare or net-wealth payback test.
Affordability
The denominator is growing Republic GNI*, not all-island income or an EU fiscal-rule ratio. Republic macroeconomic and tax-financing feedback is not estimated.
Managed Integration examples

Optional buttons load selected real output growth paths and favourable study-based negotiation terms. They are not fitted forecasts. The separate 25-year tests report annual balance, cumulative payback and sensitivity to fiscal growth and marginal revenue.
Reproduction
The run download includes the exact inputs for the selected run and every compared bundle, the horizon, annual outputs, comparison lines and the executable SHA-256 fingerprint.
Input validation
Unsupported percentages, invalid types, unknown inputs, invalid horizons and the removed residual-shift mechanism are rejected. Interface ranges are scenario choices, not confidence intervals.
Omissions
No complete household distribution, trade, banking, currency, housing, EU-budget, actuarial or welfare model. Hybrid historical benchmarks need updated programme costing before a policy estimate.
